capabilities.verb: Keep your health records on your own server
capabilities.summary: Self-host on Linux with Docker: the database, uploaded files and task queue stay on your infrastructure, with no managed cloud tier.
proofs: Nothing phones home — data lives where you deploy it
LLM API keys are Fernet-encrypted at rest and masked in responses
Prompt-injection screening on AI input; audit log on every clinical write
Export to a FHIR Bundle or ZIP backup with a SHA256 manifest

capabilities.verb: Ask your own records questions in plain language
capabilities.summary: The chat assistant answers from your biomarkers, medications and documents with citations back to the source, and proposes every write for your approval.
proofs: Answers cite the records they draw from
Proposes, never writes: every change opens a review card you approve
Works with any OpenAI-compatible provider, including local vLLM or Ollama

capabilities.verb: Compare lab results across labs and over time
capabilities.summary: The biomarker engine normalizes results from different providers to a common unit and charts each marker longitudinally against its reference range.
proofs: Results from different labs auto-convert to a common unit
Every result is scored 0.0–1.0 inside its reference range
Trend charts flag normal versus abnormal values over time

capabilities.verb: Turn lab reports into structured, searchable data
capabilities.summary: Snap a photo or drop a PDF of a report, letter or discharge summary; an OCR + AI pipeline extracts biomarkers, medications and findings for your review.
proofs: Handles lab reports, doctor letters, imaging and discharge summaries
Magic Fill maps pasted clinical text onto structured examination fields
Extraction runs in the background worker, off the API process

capabilities.verb: Follow a pregnancy, condition or recovery across visits
capabilities.summary: Clinical events group the examinations, results and notes of one journey into a single timeline with custom fields like trimester or pain intensity.
proofs: Seeded journey types — pregnancy, pain episode, surgical recovery — carry their own field schemas
Every journey links back to the examinations and results that fed it
Journeys are stored as FHIR Condition resources, exposed on the R4 facade
Type blueprints, categories and templates localize with the app

capabilities.verb: Bring in data from wearables, apps and clinics
capabilities.summary: Bundled connectors pull wearable and hospital data — Withings over OAuth2, hospital FHIR servers over SMART-on-FHIR — and an HMAC-verified webhook receives pushes from custom senders.
proofs: Pulls records from hospital FHIR servers over SMART-on-FHIR with PKCE
The bundled Withings connector pulls weight, blood pressure, heart rate and SpO2 over OAuth2
The inbound webhook verifies HMAC-SHA256 signatures with replay protection
Official bridge client SDKs ship for Python, TypeScript and Kotlin
An MCP client connection exposes external tool servers to the assistant

capabilities.verb: Put appointments on a calendar you own
capabilities.summary: Publish examinations and clinical events to Google, Microsoft 365, Nextcloud, iCloud, Fastmail, CalDAV or an ICS feed. Detail is redacted by default.
proofs: Default redaction shows only “Medical appointment” — never the reason
Full detail is opt-in and requires explicit confirmation
Credentials live in the sealed store; binding rows hold only a pointer
Inbound events are attributable-only — lookalikes need your confirmation
Providers, scopes and destinations come from a shared catalog

capabilities.verb: Get medication reminders and out-of-range alerts
capabilities.summary: Scheduled reminders and event-driven threshold alerts fan out to the in-app inbox and Web Push, with per-kind preferences and digest collapsing.
proofs: Medication and follow-up reminders fire on Celery beat schedules
Threshold alerts evaluate on observation ingestion — a bad result alerts immediately
Delivery is real-time in-app (WebSocket) and Web Push (VAPID)
Per-kind preferences with inline mute and digest collapsing

capabilities.verb: Extend it with your own integration providers
capabilities.summary: The Integration SDK authors bundled extensions: one validated manifest declares capabilities and data classes, and the engine never probes provider internals.
proofs: One validated manifest gates every declared capability at registration
BaseHealthProvider, BaseConfigFlow and ObservationBuilder ship in the SDK
OAuth2 + PKCE, rate-limit handling and cursor-based delta sync included
A ten-chapter doc set starts with a ten-minute quickstart

capabilities.verb: Integrate clinics over a standards-based FHIR R4 API
capabilities.summary: An OAuth2 + SMART-scoped FHIR R4 facade serves 20 resource types with CapabilityStatement, search Bundles, Provenance-on-write and soft-delete tombstones.
proofs: 20 R4 resources — Patient, Observation, Condition, MedicationStatement, DiagnosticReport and more
SMART-on-FHIR scopes and OAuth2 gate every external request
Every write records Provenance; deletes leave 410 Gone tombstones
Search returns FHIR Bundles with pagination and OperationOutcome errors

useCases: Compare cholesterol across two labs after switching providers — drop both PDFs, get one unit-normalized trend line scored against its reference range.
Track a pregnancy visit by visit — start the seeded journey, fill trimester fields, link each examination, read the whole timeline in one place.
Catch an out-of-range result the day it lands — threshold rules evaluate at ingest and push a Web Push alert to your phone.
Pull your hospital record onto your own server — connect the clinic's FHIR server over SMART-on-FHIR and let cursor-based sync bring new results in.
Manage your household's records under one install — one record per person, role-scoped views, per-person dashboards and journeys.
